fixes.explanation: Eliab son of Helon is a name from the tribe of Zebulun (Numbers 1:9), and he isn't in this passage. I can see why a name like that stuck with you, friend. The one God calls by name here is "…Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur…" He's from the tribe of Judah.

Right, and it's all craftsmanship. God says He has filled Bezalel with the Spirit of God, "…with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship…" Then God lists the work: designing artistic works in gold, silver and bronze, cutting gemstones and carving wood (Exodus 31:4–5). Not a word about warfare, friend.
Six it is. God says, "For six days work may be done…" Six days, friend, and then comes the rest. I've stamped a lot of cookies in my time, and I never turn down a day off.
Five is close, friend, but it's one day short. The text says, "For six days work may be done…" Then the seventh day is the Sabbath of complete rest (Exodus 31:15).

Third is one of the six days when work may be done, so it isn't the day of rest. God says, "For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest…" The day of complete rest comes after those six, friend, on the seventh.
